name: poki
description: Let AI agents operate a real iPhone. Local MCP server and agent, no jailbreak, no extra hardware.
readmeExcerpt:
Poki uses your iPhone like you do

English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Español
poki.bot

## Quick start **Let your agent install it.** Copy this to your agent: ```text Install https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki following its root AGENTS.md, including the MCP skill, and stop whenever you need me to act. ``` **Poki MCP.** Already using Claude Code, Codex, or another MCP client? Connect Poki MCP and use your own subscription. No extra model account needed. Start the server and keep it running: ```sh git clone https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki.git cd poki ./bin/setup npm start ``` Requires macOS 15 or later, full Xcode, Rust, Node.js 24+, and ffmpeg. `./bin/setup` checks for missing dependencies. The initial build takes a few minutes. Poki targets macOS. For Linux, see the community port [poki-for-linux](https://github.com/carrotciallo/poki-for-linux) ([#16](https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki/issues/16)), maintained outside this repo. Windows: community port at [scy7796/poki-for-windows](https://github.com/scy7796/poki-for-windows) (maintained by its author, not tested by us). ### Prebuilt macOS arm64 package Download `poki-v0.1.1-macos-arm64.tar.gz` from the release and run: ```sh tar -xzf poki-v0.1.1-macos-arm64.tar.gz cd poki-v0.1.1 npm ci --no-audit --no-fund npm start ``` The package includes the native bridge and idevice tools. You do not need Rust or `./bin/setup`. You still need macOS on Apple Silicon, full Xcode, Node.js 24+, Python 3, and ffmpeg. Register your MCP client and install the optional Agent as described below. In another terminal, from the same directory, register the MCP server: ```sh claude mcp add --scope user poki-mcp -- node "$PWD/src/stdio.mjs" # Claude Code codex mcp add poki-mcp -- node "$PWD/src/stdio.mjs" # Codex ``` **Poki Agent.** For Poki's standalone terminal agent or messaging channels, keep `npm start` running and open another terminal in the same directory. Install the agent, add its command to this terminal's path, and sign in: ```sh npm ci --prefix agent export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH" poki login poki status ``` Poki Agent uses GPT-6.1 Terra (`gpt-6.1-terra`) with low reasoning by default. We recommend keeping it: it is the fastest setup we have tested for phone tasks. Override it with `POKI_AGENT_MODEL`; see [Run Poki Agent](agent/README.md). For a physical iPhone, pair it with your Mac over USB first. See [Physical iPhone setup](docs/physical-iphone.md). Update with `./bin/poki update`. Set `POKI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to disable the daily anonymous GitHub release check. See [Update](AGENTS.md#update) for the request URL, restart steps, and prebuilt packages. ## Try a task With Poki Agent, one connected iPhone is selected automatically. With multiple devices, add `--device ''`. ```sh node bin/call.mjs list_devices # Find your device UUID poki "Search esp32 in Chrome and summarize the top result" ``` > **Note:** Poki controls your real iPhone. If you ask it to send messages or make payments, it will. Screen contents are sent to your configured model service. Gets faster with use: Poki Agent remembers past tasks and runs them faster on repeat. **Channels:** After configuring an authorized channel, start it with `poki imessage` or `poki telegram`. See [Poki Agent](agent/README.md) for setup. **MCP clients:** Claude Code, Codex, and any client supporting `mcpServers` JSON. Physical iPhone support has been verified only on iPhones using the Chinese interface. Physical devices support portrait orientation only. App container export and direct links to Settings subpages are unavailable. See [verification and known limits](docs/verification.md). ## Docs | Topic | Read | | --- | --- | | Installation, other MCP clients, and troubleshooting | [Install guide](docs/install.md) | | Poki Agent, models, iMessage, and Telegram | [Run Poki Agent](agent/README.md) | | MCP tool reference | [Tool behavior](docs/tools.md) | | Environment variables and sessions | [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) | | USB pairing, Developer Mode, and Wi-Fi | [Physical iPhone setup](docs/physical-iphone.md) | | Test results, known limits, and disclaimers | [Verification](docs/verification.md) | | Bridge architecture | [Native bridge](native/NATIVE.md) and [simulator adapter](native/simulator.md) | | Roadmap | [poki.bot](https://poki.bot) | ## Roadmap

## Star History ## Core contributors

ZhehanZhang
Proposed driving a physical iPhone over Tailscale in #2, the idea behind remote connections, which shipped in #8.
igc110
Found why taps on a physical iPhone were slow in #10; the fix that followed made them about a third faster.
edge369
Made Poki run on a router in #14, so Telegram can drive the iPhone with the Mac powered off; #15, #17 and #19 followed.

carrotciallo
Ported Poki to Linux and tested it on a physical iPhone over USB, LAN and Tailscale in #16; the README now points to it.
guangtouge82
Traced failing touches on a physical iPhone to a missing display service in #18; Poki now says nothing was sent and points to prepare-device.
Dreaminmaster
Fixed a corrupt cached route that aborted unrelated Agent tasks (#21, #22), then let the Agent reuse its post-action screen read in #37.

PeterKingXu1s
Reported in #25 that a natural-language stop request did not interrupt an iMessage task; Poki now replies to mid-task messages and points to /stop.
ScottH1122
Reproduced two Agent bugs in #27 and #28, disabled controls offered as tap targets and partly failed batches losing their trace; both are fixed.
jiahuipaung
Fixed in #34 a RemotePairing connection that died when the iPhone's LAN address changed (#30); a real iPhone reconnected in 768 ms.

scy7796
Fixed taps that failed every time over RemotePairing from a Windows host in #39; 5 of 5 taps then worked.

releases.name: Poki 0.2.8 (500) pre-alpha
releases.body:
Poki 0.2.8 (500) and Poki Setup 0.2.1 (307). This is the first pre-alpha of the standalone iPhone app. Poki now drives the phone, chats, talks and re-signs itself on the iPhone, so a computer is only needed for the first install. Parts are untested and may break; use Beta or Stable for daily use. Code: `standalone` branch.

> [!WARNING]
> **This build approves every action by default.** Agents can pay, delete, send messages and change settings without asking you first. Only connect agents you trust, keep an eye on the Live Activity, and turn Poki off when you're not using it.
>
> Setup › Advanced (top right) › Diagnostics › **Testing** has three switches, all off:
> - **Do not turn on Ask Before Sensitive Steps.** The manual approvals don't fully work yet.
> - **Please try Auto-Classifier** and tell us whether it works. The chat model decides each sensitive step from what you said in the chat or the live call, with no card, notification or tap. The chat shows "Approved by model" or "Not approved by model" with a short reason; say yes in the chat to let a refused step through. Permissiveness: Strict, Balanced (default) or Permissive. Changes apply the next time Poki opens.
> - **ask

releases.name: Poki v0.1.1
releases.body:
Poki now supports remote connections, and it tells you when a new version is out.

## Remote connections

### Poki now supports remote connections.

## Also in this release

- **Update notices.** Once a day, Poki checks GitHub for the latest release. When a newer version is available, `poki_mcp_status` and `poki status` display the version number, a one-line summary, the release link, and the update command. The check is anonymous and sends no tokens, device information, or conversation data. If GitHub is unreachable, Poki stays quiet and starts as usual.
- **`poki update`.** In a source checkout, this command fetches the latest code and rebuilds it using `./bin/setup`. It only runs when you are on `main` with a clean working tree. It stops without making changes if you are on another branch, have uncommitted or untracked files, or if an incoming file would overwrite an ignored file. In a prebuilt package, it prints the manual download steps. It never restarts the service automatically.
- **Restart prompt.** When the code has been updated but the service is still running the old version, Poki tells you to restart it.
- **Channels shut down cleanly.** iMessage and Telegram channel p

releases.name: Poki v0.1.0
releases.body:
First public release of Poki.

- **Poki MCP:** a local MCP server that lets your agent read and operate a real iPhone. Connect it to Claude Code, Codex, or another MCP client and use your own subscription. No extra model account needed.
- **Poki Agent:** send a task from iMessage, Telegram, or the terminal. It runs the task on your iPhone and learns reusable routes.

No jailbreak and no extra hardware.

## Install

Hand the repository to your agent, or follow [docs/install.md](https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki/blob/main/docs/install.md).

`poki-v0.1.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz` is a signed and notarized build for Apple silicon Macs. It saves the Rust toolchain and the first build. Physical iPhones still need a full Xcode installation. Requires macOS 15 or later.

SHA-256: `bbf02b8763570fde09361f6867a04c2bea72126dc452c2db61c382236dee9a1c`

Licensed under AGPL-3.0-only. Please read the [disclaimer](https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki#disclaimer) before use.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Automated agent that operates local iPhones via the Model Context Protocol without jailbreaking.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Poki allows AI agents to interact with a physical iPhone as a standard user would, completely locally. It implements a local Model Context Protocol server that translates agent intents into precise iOS actions. The system requires no extra hardware or jailbreaking to function securely. This enables complex mobile automation workflows directly driven by conversational AI models.
keyFeatures: Native Interaction: Simulates real touch events and gestures on unjailbroken iOS devices.
MCP Integration: Exposes device capabilities to AI models via the Model Context Protocol.
Local Execution: Runs the server and agent entirely locally to ensure maximum privacy.
Zero Hardware: Operates without requiring custom USB controllers or specific hardware dongles.
Workflow Automation: Translates high-level language commands into concrete application actions.
